arcs: Ritual-of-entry -> featured masthead -> operable archive -> per-work rest -> contact close (Siena, winner-verified as an SOTD/SOTM entry): the gate is a threshold you cross, the masthead is the first impression, then the archive is something you DRIVE, not read. The story is 'here is a body of work you thread by hand.'

Continuous-surface / no discrete acts (Bisous verified; KAI a single-product variant): there is no hero-then-sections seam — the whole page is one moving reel (Bisous infinite vertical slider) or one operable video field (KAI drag-scrub). The narrative arc is spatial ('keep moving through the material'), not chaptered. Caveat: only Bisous is a fully verified continuous-surface site, and it shares a studio with Bloom (Beaucoup.); treat this as a legal editorial-dark resolution rather than broad archetype canon.

Loader-as-first-scene (Bisous + Bloom, verified): the arrival is diegetic — curated visuals during load ARE the opening scene, then dissolve into the first live frame. The film starts before the site does; there is no separate 'intro then content.' Caveat: both verified instances are the same studio (Beaucoup.).
Rough-cut assembly (Grit, register-verified): torn-edge collage sequenced like a scrapbook — the arc is a montage of fragments, deliberately un-smoothed, monochrome as the unifying grade.
story.thread: The fil rouge is ONE treated-material gesture chosen at the hero and carried to the footer: (1) the film grade itself — every image the same desaturated high-contrast duotone/mono, edge-to-edge, source light kept (Siena, Grit, Bloom); (2) the operable-material mechanic — the reader's own hand drives the footage/stills (Siena hold-and-drag filmstrip; KAI drag-scrub video; Bloom operable reel) and that same drag-to-reveal verb recurs at every image the page shows; (3) the doubled-label/stochastic type texture that recurs on every heading, caption and link (Siena two-line char roll; Bisous per-letter opacity flicker). Winners pick exactly one of these three, establish it in the first viewport, and never let it go silent — the thread is felt in the loader, the hero, every mid-page figure, and the close.
story.copy: Impersonal curator voice, fragments over sentences, imperatives confined to chrome ('Hold and drag to navigate', 'Enter'). Proof is borrowed verbatim (jury/press pull-quotes) and never self-claimed. The site never narrates or credits its own construction — no 'a film about', no listing its own typefaces. Metadata is stamped as mono facts (DISCIPLINE · YEAR · RUNTIME). One register per page; the single calculated exception is Bisous' production-software 'labeled tag' chrome, which reads as diegetic craft, not a HUD mixed into editorial prose. Straight apostrophes in the dark register (Siena ').

spectacle_model.hero: The first viewport commits the grade and the thread in one frame: a full-bleed treated still or a live cinematic loader-scene, an oversized display title (type-as-image; on Siena the h1 is reportedly omitted per the internal teardown — not independently verified), a mono metadata stamp, and a pointer-events:none gradient-scrim nav. The entrance move is the signature — Siena's two-line doubled-char label roll (visible copy translate out, duplicate translateY in, short stagger, sub-second easeOutQuint per the internal teardown) or Bisous' stochastic per-letter opacity settle. The hero does not merely display; it hands the reader the verb they will reuse (drag, cross, thread) — and on drag/operable pages the cursor itself morphs to a label/glyph that names that verb (see element_states.cursor).

No section drops to pointer-dead silence; the drag verb and the grade persist to the footer.

spectacle_model.recommended_law: Two independently verified structural facts survive: (1) the hero carries the single most dominant novel mechanic and no later section introduces a rival of equal-or-greater visual dominance — later sections re-express the ONE Step-2 thread rather than adding a second wow (Siena filmstrip re-uses the doubled-char roll; Bloom re-spends via stacked-card + hover-preview); (2) no section after the hero is fully static — the failure mode this archetype punishes is silence, not a second peak. In the continuous-surface expression the hero and body fuse into one operable/looping reel with no discrete peak (Bisous verified; KAI a single-product variant) — a legal editorial-dark resolution, though the evidence for it as broad canon is thin (one fully verified site, sharing a studio with Bloom). The per-section intensity numbers used elsewhere in this playbook are ordinal authoring targets, not measured DOM reads (see unverified). Phase-4 wording: 'One thread, lived hero-to-footer; the hero owns the dominant mechanic, later sections re-express it, no section goes silent.'

algorithm.rule: Classify by content, not taste. Archive/body-of-work brief (film foundation, production house, cinematographer) -> ritual-of-entry arc (gate -> masthead -> operable archive -> rest -> close). Single-continuous-material brief (CGI studio, one craft object, one reel) -> continuous-surface arc (loader-scene -> infinite/operable reel = the whole page, no discrete sections). Rough/DIY brand -> rough-cut montage. Default to ritual-of-entry when the component library requires a discrete section chain.

algorithm.decide: The signature thread (the fil rouge carried hero-to-footer)
algorithm.rule: Choose exactly ONE family and apply it page-wide: (a) the film GRADE — one desaturated high-contrast duotone/mono on every image, edge-to-edge, source light kept, over a pure off-black floor; (b) the operable-DRAG verb — the reader's pointer/touch drives every still/video (hold-and-drag filmstrip, drag-scrub video, drag reel); (c) the type TEXTURE — a doubled two-line label roll OR a stochastic per-letter opacity flicker on every heading/caption/link. Checkable constraint: the chosen family appears in the first viewport AND recurs in every subsequent section; the other two families may appear at most once, locally, and never as a page-wide system that repeats across sections.
evidence: Siena: grade + hold-and-drag + doubled-char roll (one family)
Bisous: per-letter opacity flicker on all type + infinite reel

algorithm.rule: Ritual-of-entry -> gated-splash(threshold) + hero-masthead(climax) + pinned-filmstrip(reel) + editorial-split(per-work detail) + close-panel + oversized-wordmark footer. Continuous-surface -> loader-scene + fullscreen-vertical-reel (GAP: infinite bidirectional slider) as the whole body + curtain-less transitions + bare-cue/costumed-credits footer. Never open on a card grid; never a centered-hero + twin-CTA; lateral or continuous motion is hand-driven or IS the content, never an autoplay carousel.
evidence: Bisous infinite vertical reel is the home

algorithm.decide: Momentum map (dominant hero mechanic, no rival, no silence)
algorithm.rule: Deterministic constraints, ranked by animated-area x displacement (a proxy a composer can evaluate against the built DOM, not a taste call): (1) the hero holds the single most dominant novel mechanic on the page; (2) NO section after the hero introduces a NEW mechanic whose animated-area x displacement equals or exceeds the hero's — later sections re-express the Step-2 thread, they add no rival; (3) NO section is static: every section after the hero must exhibit at least one of {the chosen thread applied to its imagery, the operable-drag verb, an entrance or hover motion on its type/figures} — a section with no entrance motion, no hover state, and no operable media is illegal; (4) the reel/proof section runs the operable-drag verb continuously; the per-work detail may reduce to the grade + one type signature but never to none; the close re-expresses the thread exactly once. Continuous-surface: constraints (1)-(2) collapse to 'one surface that never stops moving and introduces no rival mechanic.' The ordinal intensity targets (hero highest, reel near-hero, detail reduced-but-nonzero, close single re-expression) live in section_playbook as authoring intent, not as measured units.

algorithm.rule: hero-masthead: h1 -> kinetic-reveal OR (signature) doubled masked-label-swap; media(back) -> scrub-film OR clip-reveal + grain-grade overlay; data-strip -> mono stamp; on drag/operable pages, cursor -> verb-label morph (GAP). reel: pinned-filmstrip (desktop hold-and-drag) + swipe-snap-gallery (mobile native snap); index rows -> hover-preview-video (GAP: reveal the muted footage on row hover); caption -> text-emphasis-fill. detail: editorial-split, media left, h2 -> char-assemble, prose -> text-emphasis-fill + semantic-accent, media -> image-curtain (grayscale->colour reveal, so the reveal itself runs the grade transition), spec -> counter-odometer. close: close-panel, ask -> kinetic-reveal, channels -> accent-link + masked-label-swap. Use image-curtain (not plain clip-reveal) on every graded image.

algorithm.rule: cta -> full-token ink-inversion fill (fill-invert-cta; never a pale tint) + optional two-line label roll (masked-label-swap), sub-second ease-signature. link -> accent recolor + underline wipe from origin-left (accent-link), ~.2s. figure -> contained zoom scale(1.1) inside overflow:hidden + companion cue (figure-hover); gallery -> focus-defocus siblings; operable/index variant -> hover-preview-video (reveal muted footage). index_row -> row lights accent rule + surfaced meta with siblings dimmed (index-row-hover) OR, for a body-of-film-work, the footage-preview reveal (hover-preview-video). heading -> masked reveal on entrance only, NO hover on in-flow headings (consistent with the Siena/Truekind entries; exact rules from an internal teardown). nav -> transparent + gradient scrim, ink-inversion by section behind, show-on-scroll-up; never frosted, never a contrasting border-bottom. cursor -> on drag/operable fields, morph to a verb-label/glyph ('DRAG'/'HOLD'/'VIEW'/play-triangle) that teaches the operable verb (GAP: cursor-verb-label).

algorithm.rule: Pointer classes go dormant (pointer-parallax, magnetic-cursor, focus-defocus, conic-border-shine — native/off on touch). Press-class elements answer the tap with a 90-160ms flash floor (fill-invert-cta :active). The hold-and-drag filmstrip and any horizontal reel switch to native scroll-snap + OS momentum (swipe-snap-gallery) with next-cell peek and snap dots. Drag-scrub video answers touch-drag natively (KAI). Index hover-preview switches to tap-to-play-inline vs navigate (the footage reveal has no hover on touch). The cursor verb-label has no touch equivalent — replace it with a persistent 'swipe'/'drag' hint or a next-cell peek as the verb teacher. Figures get tap-to-enlarge. Grain-grade and any shader ground stay but drop amplitude. Bisous' infinite vertical reel = native touch swipe.

cta.hover: Full-token ink-inversion FILL — outline/light button floods a solid brand value, label flips to the opposite ink (Siena's CTA floods to solid, nested arrow inverting the opposite way, sub-second easeOutQuint per the internal teardown). Signature hero CTA adds a two-line label roll (visible translate out, duplicate translateY in, short stagger). Never a pale tint. The exact selectors/values are from an internal teardown, not independently verified; the ink-inversion-fill mechanic itself is standard.
cta.tap: The fill IS the tap answer — :active flash 90-160ms floor; no separate hover-only reveal.
cta.focus: :focus-visible mirrors hover (same fill/inversion) plus an ink/accent ring; reachable in keyboard order.

link.hover: Accent recolor + underline wipe drawn from origin-left (scaleX 0->1, transform-origin left; Anthropic text-decoration-color transparent->ink ~.2s, text-underline-offset varies by context). Bisous menu links: randomized per-letter transformation. The underline-wipe selector referenced from Truekind is a cross-archetype micro-interaction borrow (Truekind is a light skincare SOTD, not dark cinematic-editorial) and is not independently verified — the mechanic is generic; the citation is not editorial-dark canon (see unverified).
link.tap: Instant recolor + underline present (no drawn animation needed on touch).
link.focus: Underline shown + accent colour; offset matches its context.

figure.hover: Contained zoom scale(1.1) inside overflow:hidden (Siena figure zoom) + one companion cue (caption rise, scrim lift, or tint) — felt, never a 1-3% twitch. Gallery variant: hovered figure sharpens while siblings blur+dim (focus-defocus). Operable variant: hover/drag scrubs the footage (KAI). Index/project-row variant: hover reveals the muted footage preview (hover-preview-video), often cursor-tracking.
figure.tap: Tap-to-enlarge or navigate; drag scrubs on the operable variant (native touch-drag); index footage-preview becomes tap-to-play-inline vs navigate on touch.
figure.focus: focus-within triggers the same zoom + cue so keyboard users reach revealed captions.

index_row.hover: For a body-of-film-work, the canonical reveal is the footage itself: hover a title/row and its muted video/still previews inline (hover-preview-video), commonly cursor-tracking. Fallback / text-only lists: the row lights an accent rule + surfaces metadata while siblings dim to ~45% (index-row-hover; Depo Luxe, Son Daven, Siena). ~.3s on ease-signature.
index_row.tap: Navigate on tap, or tap-to-play-inline for the footage-preview variant; brief press flash; no sibling-dim / no hover-preview on touch (pointer-driven reveals are dormant).
index_row.focus: :focus-visible lights the row (or shows a poster frame) identically; siblings dim so the focused target is unambiguous.

heading.hover: NONE on in-flow headings — consistent with the Siena/Truekind entries (their published hover rules do not touch body prose, in-flow headings, or numerals; exact rules from an internal teardown). Hover on titles happens only inside a card/index-row context.
heading.focus: n/a; entrance is the only motion — masked line reveal (kinetic-reveal, power4.out) or per-char assemble (char-assemble) or stochastic per-letter opacity settle (Bisous), fire-once, opacity holds 1 (a mask, never a fade).

nav.hover: Links recolor/underline (accent-link) or per-char rollover (split-rollover). Bar itself: transparent gradient scrim over the hero, gains ground on scroll, ink-inversion by the section behind (pointer-events:none scrim, .on-dark flips ink). Never frosted, never a contrasting border-bottom.
nav.tap: Menu toggle opens the dual-menu/overlay; links answer tap with instant recolor.
nav.focus: show-on-scroll-up reveals the bar; focus-visible rings on links; the pointer-events:none scrim never traps focus.

cursor.hover: On drag/operable fields (filmstrip, drag-scrub video, reel) the cursor morphs from the default pointer to a verb-label or glyph that names the operable verb — 'DRAG', 'HOLD', 'VIEW', or a play-triangle — so the affordance is taught visually, not only by onboarding copy. Enters on pointer-over the operable field, retracts to default on exit (cursor-verb-label GAP).
cursor.tap: n/a — no cursor on touch; replaced by a persistent 'swipe'/'drag' hint or a next-cell peek (see mobile_answer).
cursor.focus: n/a — decorative pointer layer; keyboard reaches the operable content via the underlying controls, never via the cursor glyph.

mobile_answer: Pointer classes go dormant (pointer-parallax, magnetic-cursor, focus-defocus, conic-border-shine are fine-pointer only; depth comes from scroll on touch). Press-class elements carry the load: fill-invert-cta answers the tap with a 90-160ms flash floor; index rows navigate with a brief press flash and no sibling-dim. The desktop hold-and-drag filmstrip and every horizontal reel switch to native scroll-snap + OS momentum via swipe-snap-gallery (next-cell peek, enhancer-fed snap dots — the verbatim-scored Awwwards Mobile Excellence line, zero JS physics). KAI's drag-scrub video answers touch-drag natively; Bisous' infinite vertical reel is a native touch swipe. Index footage-preview switches from hover to tap-to-play-inline vs navigate. The cursor verb-label has no touch equivalent — replace it with a persistent 'swipe'/'drag' hint or a next-cell peek that teaches the verb. Figures switch to tap-to-enlarge. Grain-grade and any shader ground stay but drop amplitude; reduced-motion degrades scrubbed media to a static graded poster.

seen_in: Awwwards catalog: 'Video Hover Preview', 'Project hover preview' (Olivier Gillaizeau), 'Cursor hover preview video player (Canvas)', Bittercreek.Studio index hover
gaps.mechanic: The table-stakes production-house index interaction: hovering a project title/row reveals its muted footage (video or still sequence) inline, commonly cursor-tracking (the preview follows or anchors near the pointer), a marquee/scrolling title gliding over it. For an archetype whose content IS a body of film work this is the single most canonical index reveal, and it is stronger than the text-only spotlight-dim the index_row state currently encodes. Compositor-friendly (muted autoplay video or sprite/still crossfade). Touch answer: no hover — tap-to-play-inline vs navigate, or a poster frame. Reduced-motion: static poster frame, no autoplay.

A full-screen vertical slider that IS the whole home — infinite scroll in BOTH vertical directions (looping, no start/end), one full-bleed treated work per panel, titles composed as studio-name + client-name. Continuous project-to-project flow with no discrete sections; the macrostructure itself is the spectacle-continuation. Native touch-swipe on mobile; wheel/drag on desktop with eased momentum (Lenis-smoothed). Reduced-motion: static stacked panels, native scroll. Fills the archetype's continuous-surface arc that every current recipe (all discrete-section chains) cannot express. Evidence caveat: one fully verified instance (Bisous), sharing a studio with Bloom (Beaucoup.) — a legal resolution, not broad canon.

Grab-drag over a video field maps pointer/touch delta to video.currentTime. Extends scrub-film (currently scroll/pointer-position -> currentTime on a single still) with: horizontal/vertical drag, a whole-SECTION operable field (not one figure), and cross-browser scrub encoding guidance — H.264 baseline, ~12-frame keyframe interval (`-g 12`) for seekability vs file size, WebCodecs fallback (mediabunny) for sample-accurate seeking in Firefox. Release momentum/inertia is an OPTIONAL enhancement — the KAI Codrops source documents only `video.currentTime = sec`, no momentum (see unverified); do not assert inertia as verified. Optional WebGL line depth-of-field is a delegated shader layer, noted not built. Native touch-drag on mobile; reduced-motion -> static poster frame.

seen_in: Awwwards cursor resources: 'Customize your mouse cursor: inspirational examples & implementation tricks', 'Hovers, Cursors and Cute Interactions' collection, 'Drag, Gestures & Other Interactions' collection
gaps.mechanic: The visual teacher for the operable verb the playbook's own thesis relies on ('the hero hands the reader the verb'). On pointer-over an operable field (filmstrip, drag-scrub video, reel) the cursor morphs from default to a verb-label/glyph — 'DRAG', 'HOLD', 'VIEW', or a play-triangle — retracting on exit. Currently the playbook teaches the verb only via onboarding COPY and lists magnetic-cursor merely as a dormant-on-touch pointer class, never as the verb-signal. Compositor-only (a fixed element tracking pointer coords, transform/opacity). Touch: no cursor — replace with a persistent 'swipe'/'drag' hint or next-cell peek. Reduced-motion: static default cursor + the onboarding copy alone.

Stochastic per-letter opacity settle: characters fade in on RANDOMIZED opacity transitions (not a uniform mask, not char-assemble's positional stagger, not scramble's charset noise) — echoing the imperfection of a 3D render / film grain on type. Entrance-once on headings/captions; a hover-replay variant fires 'randomized letter transformations' on menu links. Distinct dark-cinematic text texture our text kit (kinetic-reveal / char-assemble / text-emphasis-fill / scramble-decode) does not cover. aria-label preserves the accessible name; reduced-motion -> instant full opacity.

A pinned deck where layered cards overlap and peel as the track scrolls — each card pins, the next rises to cover/offset it, giving a mid-page mechanic that re-spends hero momentum in the proof/services band. Compositor-only (transform/opacity), reversible on scroll-back. Distinct from card-list (static grid). Mobile: native scroll with reduced overlap or a simple stack. Reduced-motion: flat stacked list.

A curtain-LESS route/section transition that leads 'seamlessly into the next work' — the opposite of curtain-transition's cover wipe. Shared-element / cross-dissolve morph where the outgoing figure flows into the incoming one, 'fluid and almost imperceptible', keeping immersion unbroken. Partially adjacent to Cyd Stumpel's View-Transitions shared-element morph already in recipes, but here it is a continuous-immersion mode with no cover phase. Reduced-motion / no-View-Transitions: instant cut.
